small_guidance:
- The fused conv+softmax+pool kernel recomputes the full conv for each of the P^3=8 pool positions; OC=16, IC=3, K=3 makes the inner GEMM tiny. Try BLOCK_C=16 (=OC) with num_warps=2 and num_stages=3, and hoist the bias load + weight tile [OC, IC*KD*KH*KW] outside the pool-window loops so the 8 conv evaluations share one weight load.
- Add a `triton.autotune` over (num_warps ∈ {1,2,4}, num_stages ∈ {2,3,4}) keyed on (N, OD, OH, OW); the program is very small (1 output voxel × 16 channels) so 1–2 warps may be optimal and free up occupancy.
- Restructure the grid so program_id covers (n, od, oh) and have each program loop over OW (or tile a few OWs together) — this amortizes weight loads across spatially adjacent outputs that share input rows.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM: precompute (or implicitly index) the unfolded input [N*D_conv*H_conv*W_conv, IC*KD*KH*KW] and do a tiled matmul against weight^T [IC*KD*KH*KW, OC]. With OC=16 the N-tile of the GEMM is the full channel dim, so use BLOCK_M=64 (spatial), BLOCK_N=16 (OC), BLOCK_K=27 (IC*K^3) — one shot, no recompute across the pool window.
- Split into two kernels with a small intermediate: (1) conv-only GEMM writing a [N, OC, D_conv, H_conv, W_conv] buffer in channels-last so OC is contiguous; (2) a fused softmax+maxpool(4) kernel that, for each (n, od, oh, ow), gathers the 4×4×4=64 pre-softmax vectors of length OC, applies softmax per voxel, and reduces max over the 64 voxels. This avoids the 8× conv recomputation that currently dominates.
- Alternatively, fuse conv+softmax+pool but at the granularity of one program per (n, od, oh, ow) that first computes and caches all P^3 conv outputs (P^3 × OC = 128 fp32 in registers/SMEM), then does softmax+max in a single pass — eliminates the redundant weight×input work without an intermediate tensor.
